G3 · Spell rows · Claude review of the scratch mockups · 11 November 2026

Review of the three G3 mockups

ChatGPT's boards were read in full and re-measured on the unchanged live build. Each finding below shows today's screen, ChatGPT's proposal and, where I would change it, my alternative. Green border marks the one I recommend. Nothing here is built; these are scratch treatments of the real app in an isolated browser.

Short version. 1 — ChatGPT's dialog is right; I add counts that update as you tick. 2 and 3 — I recommend a different spell row (C): the same height as ChatGPT's Quiet option on a phone while still showing "School spell", no extra height at all on a laptop, and Remove stays in the corner where every other card has it.
8b.1-UI-01

Review starting spells

ChatGPT's proposal already uses the option card the app's other pickers use (measured against Paragon's: same border, radius and font), puts Later and Confirm together below a divider, and keeps them in view while a long list scrolls. I would keep all of that.

What I add. Today, and in ChatGPT's version, "Given · 3 left" never changes while you tick — you count for yourself and only learn you went over when Confirm refuses. In mine each group shows a running count, turns solid when it is complete and red with "deselect 1" when it is over. The headings use the same serif bold as the pickers and the next screen, and "Given" reads "Given by your School" as that next screen does.

Long list and laptop, with the counts

Checked on the scratch build at both widths: Later closes and writes nothing; Confirm with eight spells leaves Jurojin's Balm as a reward and offers only the Earth choice; an over-count Confirm is still refused with nothing written; every option is 44 px tall; the action bar does not move when the list scrolls (754 px on phone before and after).

Decision 1: approve ChatGPT's layout with the live counts (recommended), approve it without them, or revise.
8b.1-UI-02 and 8b.1-UI-03

The spell row

ChatGPT's two options both fix the problems. My concerns with them, measured:

  • Height. Every spell card grows from 148 px to 200 px (A) or 229 px (B) on a phone — and by the same amount on a laptop, where the name already had 775 px and nothing needed to move.
  • Remove moves. On every other card in the app (Techniques, Advantages, Disadvantages) the × sits in the top-right corner. ChatGPT's row gives spells alone a boxed × at the end of the Cast line, which also makes Remove the heaviest control on the card.
  • B spends a whole line on two words.

Option C. On a phone the name takes the first line with the × beside it in its usual corner; Cast, the help button and Memorised take the second line, and "School spell" sits at the end of that same line as a quiet tag (the app's existing tag style). On a laptop the row stays one line, as today, with the corner kept clear. Rewards show no tag. With more than one School the tag names the School instead.

Heights in CSS pixels with a two-line description. C gives the name 42 px less than A/B in Manage (the × sits beside it); the longest name in the spell catalogue, "Wrath of Kaze-no-Kami (Hurricane)", still shows in full, and in Play the name has the full 298 px. A starting Kitsu holds nine spells: on a phone that list is about 1332 px today, 2032 px with B and 1782 px with C.

Checked on the scratch build at both widths: a tap on the Memorised label changes only that spell; a tap on the outer edge of the × removes only that reward; a renamed reward survives save-and-reapply; Play keeps the name read-only, Memorised locked and × hidden; saved spell records are identical before and after every treatment; no page errors.

The two findings stay separate decisions

Decision 2 (name and School cue): C (recommended), ChatGPT's A, ChatGPT's B, or revise.
Decision 3 (Remove and Memorised): C — × stays in its corner with the corner kept clear (recommended), ChatGPT's boxed × on the Cast line, or revise.
